title: The conormal module of a relative global complete intersection is free on the equations
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n,c\ge0$ integers and $f_1,\dots,f_c\in P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] such that $S=P/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ is a relative global complete intersection over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection]. Let $I=(f_1,\dots,f_c)\subseteq P$; the conormal module $I/I^2$ is an $S=P/I$-module. Then $I/I^2$ is a free $S$-module [def-weil-pbc-free-module] with basis the classes $f_1\bmod I^2,\dots,f_c\bmod I^2$; in particular $I/I^2\cong S^{\oplus c}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00SV (lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection-conormal, line 36767), part (3); tag verified in stacks-project/tags/tags (00SV,algebra-lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection-conormal)

proof.text: (Reduction to a map.) Write $I=(f_1,\dots,f_c)\subseteq P$, $\pi:P\to S=P/I$ the quotient map, $N=I/I^2$ and $e_j=f_j\bmod I^2\in N$. $N$ is a $P$-module killed by $I$, hence an $S$-module with $\pi(p)\cdot(x\bmod I^2)=px\bmod I^2$. Let $\varphi:S^{\oplus c}\to N$ be the $S$-linear map $(s_1,\dots,s_c)\mapsto\sum_js_je_j$. By the definition of a basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module], $e_1,\dots,e_c$ is a basis of $N$ if and only if $\varphi$ is bijective, and then $\varphi$ is an isomorphism $S^{\oplus c}\cong N$. So it suffices to show that $\varphi$ is bijective.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00SV (lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection-conormal, line 36767), proof of (3), lines 36834-36839

proof.text: (Localizing at a prime of $S$.) Fix a prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset S$, let $\mathfrak q'=\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, a prime of $P$ containing $I$, $U=P\setminus\mathfrak q'$, $B=P_{\mathfrak q'}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $J=IB$, the ideal of $B$ generated by $f_1/1,\dots,f_c/1$. (a) By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient] the map $\lambda:B\to S_{\mathfrak q}$, $p/u\mapsto\pi(p)/\pi(u)$, is surjective with kernel $J$, so $B/J\cong S_{\mathfrak q}$. (b) Since $\pi$ is surjective and $\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak q'$, $\pi(U)=S\setminus\mathfrak q$; an element $u\in U$ acts on $N$ as $\pi(u)$, so the localization $N_{\mathfrak q}$ of the $S$-module $N$ at $S\setminus\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] is the localization $U^{-1}N$ of the $P$-module $N$ (the same fractions $x/\pi(u)=x/u$ and the same relation $u''(u_2x_1-u_1x_2)=0$ with $u''\in U$), and its $S_{\mathfrak q}$-module structure is the $B$-module structure through $\lambda$. (c) Localizing at $U$ the exact sequences of $P$-modules $0\to I\to P$ and $0\to I^2\to I\to N\to0$ gives exact sequences [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact]: $U^{-1}I\to B$ is injective with image $J$, the image of $U^{-1}(I^2)$ in it is $I^2B=J^2$, so $U^{-1}N\cong J/J^2$, $(x\bmod I^2)/u\mapsto(x/u)\bmod J^2$, an isomorphism of $B$-modules. Hence $N_{\mathfrak q}\cong J/J^2$ compatibly with $S_{\mathfrak q}\cong B/J$ of (a), and $e_j/1\in N_{\mathfrak q}$ corresponds to the class of $f_j/1$ in $J/J^2$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00SV (lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection-conormal, line 36767), proof of (3), lines 36834-36839

proof.text: (The local basis.) By [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-local-regular-sequence] (Stacks 00SV (1); $S$ is a relative global complete intersection and $\mathfrak q'$ is the inverse image of the prime $\mathfrak q$ of $S$), $f_1/1,\dots,f_c/1$ is a regular sequence in $B=P_{\mathfrak q'}$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], generating the ideal $J$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-conormal-free] (Stacks 00LN, regular implies quasi-regular, in degree 1) the $B/J$-module $J/J^2$ is free [def-weil-pbc-free-module] with basis the classes of $f_1/1,\dots,f_c/1$. Transporting along the compatible isomorphisms of step 2, the $S_{\mathfrak q}$-module $N_{\mathfrak q}$ is free with basis $e_1/1,\dots,e_c/1$: this is the sentence of the source 'By Lemma 00LN and (1) we know that $e_1,\dots,e_c$ is a basis of $N_{\mathfrak q}$'.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00SV (lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection-conormal, line 36767), proof of (3), lines 36834-36839

proof.text: ($\varphi_{\mathfrak q}$ is bijective.) The localization of $S^{\oplus c}$ at $S\setminus\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] is $S_{\mathfrak q}^{\oplus c}$ via $(s_1,\dots,s_c)/u\mapsto(s_1/u,\dots,s_c/u)$ (localization commutes with finite direct sums: both sides have the same fractions and the same relation coordinatewise). Under this identification $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}((s_j)/u)=\sum_js_je_j/u=\sum_j(s_j/u)(e_j/1)$, i.e. $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}:S_{\mathfrak q}^{\oplus c}\to N_{\mathfrak q}$ is $(t_j)\mapsto\sum_jt_j(e_j/1)$, which is bijective because $e_1/1,\dots,e_c/1$ is a basis of $N_{\mathfrak q}$ (step 3, [def-weil-pbc-free-module]).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00SV (lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection-conormal, line 36767), proof of (3), lines 36834-36839

proof.text: (Conclusion.) Every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $S$ is prime, so by step 4 $\varphi_{\mathfrak m}$ is bijective for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-linear-map-bijective-at-maximal-localizations] (Stacks 00HN (6)) applied to the ring $S$ and $\varphi:S^{\oplus c}\to N$, $\varphi$ is bijective. By step 1, $N=I/I^2$ is a free $S$-module with basis $f_1\bmod I^2,\dots,f_c\bmod I^2$ and $I/I^2\cong S^{\oplus c}$. (If $S=0$ there is no maximal ideal and the conclusion holds trivially: $S^{\oplus c}=0=N$.)
